headline: Read-level and sketch-based methods reduce compute cost in viral sequence inference
label: Viral Genomics Inference Methods
summary: Recent preprints and a published tool report speedups from 2.1-6.6x up to ~40,000-fold by working directly on reads, seeds, or sketches.
synthesis: The common thread is reducing the computational cost of viral and related sequence inference by avoiding full alignment or exhaustive comparison and working at the level of reads, seeds, or sketches. bronko detects viral SNPs, indels and minor variants directly from reads without alignment, with near-linear scaling in sequencing depth. TurboANI estimates average nucleotide identity using SIMD seeding and bitset minwise hashing, reporting up to ~40,000-fold speedup. EMtrace runs offline on a laptop, classifying nanopore reads, estimating abundance via expectation-maximisation, and assembling consensus genomes. RabbitCD-HIT addresses protein sequence clustering at billion scale with distributed greedy incremental clustering, reporting 2.1-6.6x speedup over CD-HIT. What is new is the explicit targeting of tractable inference at the read, seed, or sketch level. The items differ in data modality and task, so this describes the dominant emphasis rather than a shared method.
